boss.brood.text: Up from the husks, my little ones!
Out of the walls! Mother calls!
Wake, wake. Someone has come to play.
My brood never sleeps when I call.
Come, small ones. Show them the count.

boss.burrow.text: Down to the roots of the hill.
The floor is mine, child. All of it.

boss.crush.text: The stone breaks you, for once.
Feel the whole hill come down.

boss.defeat.text: My children... into the walls... hide...
So this is how a shell feels... when it breaks...
Tell them... Mother is in the stone now...
Every one of us... will know... your step...

boss.hurt.text: That stung, little one. Do it again and I'll mind.
Old shells crack. New ones grow.
You hit like a pickaxe. Clumsy, and far too often.
A scratch. I have had a thousand.
Again? Well. You have my full attention now.

boss.keen.text: Listen. Listen to all of them.
A thousand little voices, child. All at once.
Cover your ears. It won't help.
This is what the walls say when you break them.

boss.last.text: The last molt. You should not have made me do this.
Everything I have left. Every scale. Every child.
The walls themselves will fight you now.

boss.rain.text: My scales are sharper than they look.
Stand still. It makes it easier.
Every one of these was mine once.

boss.rest.text: Back to the dais. The Hollow keeps.
Run, then. Tell them what you saw.
The stair goes up. So did you. Wise.

boss.shed.text: Enough. Off with the old shell.
You've cracked it. Now meet what grew underneath.
Watch closely. Nobody alive has seen me molt.
I shed my skin for the clan once. I'll shed it for you now.

boss.slayer.text: You killed {mother}. I felt her go cold through a mile of stone.
{mother} was my sister. You will not do to me what you did to her.
I know your step. It's the one that walked out of {mother}'s hollow.
{mother} sent me a last whisper through the rock. It was your name.
They say {mother} fell to you. They say a great many things.
So you're the one who put {mother} in the dust. Come and try it twice.

boss.sweep.text: The old shell remembers how to swing.
Every segment of it. All at once.

boss.wake.text: Children, wake. We have a guest.
I smelled you on the stair, stone-breaker. Every step.
You came all this way to the bottom of the world. To me.
So this is the one my little ones whisper about.
I have slept under this hill for forty winters. Wake me gently next time.
Closer. Let me see the hands that crush my children.
You walked past the shells of my brood to get here. I counted.
Welcome to the Hollow. Nobody leaves it by the stair.

boss.win.text: Hush now. Into the stone with you.
Rest. The little ones will tidy up.
You came down the stair. You won't go back up it.
That is the count settled, for one stone-breaker.

defeat.text: Count me, then. Someone's counting you.
Back to the wall... back to the dust...
Grey to grey... stone to stone...
You'll find us in every wall you break.
Not the last. Never the last.
Somewhere under your house... someone heard that.
Curl up... go quiet... like the little ones do...
Out of scales... out of... everything...
A Warden falls... and a hundred Scuttlers wake.

disguise.greet.any.text: Good day! Don't mind me, I'm only resting my legs. All of them.
Oh, hello! You're the first soul I've seen in days. The first one walking upright, anyway.
Hello, friend. Where are you headed? No, truly, I'd like to know. Exactly where.
Well met. I'm {name}. Just a wanderer. Nobody in particular. That's rather the point of me.
Don't mind me, I'm only waiting. For what? Oh, nothing much. Someone like you, perhaps.
Lovely to meet you. I'd shake your hand, but you never know where a hand's been. Yours, for instance. Underground, mostly.
Funny, I was only just thinking about you. Well, not you. Someone very like you. With a pick.
Mind how you go, friend. Lots of holes about these days. Lots of people making them.
On your own, are you? Nobody waiting for you anywhere? Ah. Good to know.
Good day, {player}. Hm? Oh, I must have heard it somewhere. Folk talk about you. Little folk.
Did you sleep well? I never sleep well above ground. Out of doors, I mean. Out in the open.
Hello! I'm just a simple villager out on a simple walk, thinking simple thoughts. What are yours?
Ever get the feeling something's watching you from the walls? No? Never mind. A pleasure to meet you.
Greetings! I've been counting the travellers on this road. You make... well. It's a number. Never mind the number.
You've come a long way, I can tell. Heels worn through, and you favour your left side. Sorry. I notice things.
Isn't it nice, being out in the open? Some find it a bit bright. Not me. I love it. Truly I do.
Oh, good, company. Tell me, do you do much mining? Only curious. Everybody has a hobby.
Peace, friend, I'm harmless. Small and harmless. Ask anyone who ever stepped on me.
Mind if I walk with you a while? I'm good company. Quiet. You'll hardly know I'm there. Nobody ever does.
Strange to meet a stranger out here. I suppose you're thinking the same of me. Only one of us is right.
What a lucky meeting, out here in the middle of nowhere. Lucky for one of us, anyway.
Bless me, a traveller! Sit, sit. Not on the stones, they're cold. Well. They're cold to you.

disguise.greet.cold.text: Brr! Come stand by me, out of the wind. I don't feel the cold much myself. I grew up somewhere colder. And darker.
Snow hides everything, doesn't it? Footprints, holes, old stones, people. I find it very restful.
Out in this, on foot? You must be on an errand. Or digging for something. Which is it?
I'd offer you a fire, but I've nothing to burn, and I don't much care for the light anyway.
Don't mind the frost on me, I've been standing here a while. Waiting for the weather to turn. Or for somebody.
The spruce folk say the ground freezes solid in winter. It doesn't, you know. Not all the way down. Things keep moving down there.
Lost in all this white? Stay close. I know every stone under this snow. I've counted them.
Cold hands? Tuck them in your sleeves. I keep mine in mine. I keep a lot of things in my sleeves.
A long way from any hearth, aren't we? The two of us, out here, with nobody to see.
Listen. The snow's so quiet you can hear the whole world under it, if you lie still. Scratching away.
Fine furs. And a fine pick, too, chipped right down to the haft. A busy winter, was it?
Ho there! I was starting to talk to the stones. They don't answer. Not so anyone up here could hear, anyway.
Careful on the ice, friend. It cracks long before it breaks. Most things do, if you've the ears for it.

disguise.greet.green.text: A friendly face on a quiet road! You'd be surprised how many folk walk straight past me and never notice I'm here.
Good road for walking, this. Some folk cut right through the hills instead. Rude to the hills, I always think.
Hello! I've been watching the road a good long while. You're the first one along who looked interesting.
Fine old woods. Old stumps, old stones. I like to turn the stones over and see who's living underneath.
Mind the path, it's full of beetles. Little things. I never step on little things. Do you?
Grand old trees, these. Their roots go right down into the stone and hold on. Some things hold on whatever you do to them.
You came from the village back there, didn't you? The one with the stone well. Lovely well. Deep. I know it from the bottom up.
Where's the road taking you, friend? Somewhere with a cellar, I hope. I'm very fond of cellars.
Pretty meadow, isn't it? Not a stone in it, if you don't look closely. There's always a stone, if you look closely.
A walker's legs and a miner's hands. That's an unusual pair, friend. Which do you use more?
Have you come far? Over the hills, or under them?
Stop a while, stop a while! The flowers don't mind. The bees don't mind. Nothing out here minds me at all.
Bless you for stopping. Most travellers on this road are in such a hurry to get underground.

disguise.greet.sand.text: Hot enough to bake bread on the rocks, isn't it? You'd think nothing could live out here. You'd be surprised what keeps cool under the sand.
Every grain of this sand was a stone once, you know. Somebody broke it. Somebody's always breaking something.
Water? Kind of you, but no. I don't need much. Never have.
Mind the dunes, friend. Folk come out here digging for the old temples, and the ground remembers who dug.
Good day! Where are you bound? East? West? Down?
You've sand in your boots and stone dust on your sleeves. Busy hands, for a walker.
The badlands keep their colours in stripes, one stripe for every year. I like a land that keeps count.
I'd offer you shade, but the only shade out here is underneath things. It's very pleasant, underneath things.
Watch out for husks, and for holes. Mostly the holes. You never know who's at the bottom of one.
Funny, meeting someone in all this empty. I'm told I'm hard to spot. Grey on gold, you'd think it would be easy.
You walk heavy, traveller. Out here the sand carries every footstep a long way down.
Sandstone, they call it. As if the stone's gone soft and sleepy in the sun. It hasn't. It's only waiting.
Lost in the dunes? No shame in it. The dunes wander about. The stone underneath never does, and neither do some of us.
Ho there! Come for the cactus fruit, or the buried rooms? Everyone comes for the buried rooms, sooner or later.

disguise.greet.stone.text: Steep climb, isn't it? Catch your breath. The mountain isn't going anywhere, and neither is anything inside it.
Careful on this stretch. Some of the stone up here is rotten. It breaks far too easily, and what's inside isn't always rock.
Lovely view, this. You can see every hole anyone's ever dug in that hillside. I like to know where they all are.
That's a fine pick on your belt. Well worn, too. I'd love to hear where it's been.
The goats won't come near this bit of the pass. Clever animals, goats. They can hear the stone breathing.
Up from the caves, were you? They run for miles under here. Ever wonder who's down in them while you're up top?
Sit, if you like. Not on that rock. Or that one. They're spoken for.
Mind your step. Every stone up here is somebody's home. My mother always said so, and she'd know.
You came up the long way, over the top. Most folk just tunnel straight through these days, whatever's in the way.
Grey rock, grey sky, grey old me. I blend right in, don't I? Ha! Sit a while.
People get lost up here all the time. The mountain never loses anyone, mind. It knows exactly where they all are.
Hello, friend. Don't mind the grit on my coat. The wind blows it about. Mostly the wind.
These hills are hollow, you know. Full of little rooms, full of little lives. Best walk softly.

disguise.reply.curious.text: How long have you been here?
What did you mean by that?

disguise.reply.polite.text: I'd best be on my way.
Kind of you to say so.

disguise.reply.suspicious.text: Why are you out here alone?
Why were you waiting for me?
How do you know so much?

fight.burrow.text: Down I go. Guess where I come up.
You dig for a living? Watch how it's really done.
Knives first. The rest of me after.
Too close, much too close. Bye now!
Brace yourself. I come up heavy.

fight.call.text: Come out, come out. Someone here knows your family.
Cousins in the wall! To me!
You know these ones. You've met their families. Under your boot.
Up from the stone, little silver!
Out of the walls! Supper's standing right there.
Swarm, little ones. This one's on the count.
Crack the stone and see who's home!

fight.dodge.text: You swing like a miner. Straight down and dull.
We don't stand still to be crushed.
Like swatting at a crack in the wall.
Hit where I'm going, not where I was.
Silverfish don't get stepped on twice.
Keep your distance. I'll keep mine.

fight.flee.text: Run, then. We're under every road you take.
Far enough? Nothing is far enough.
Go on. We'll find you by the noise you make digging.
You can leave this place. You can't leave the stone.
Running back to your tunnels? We'll be there first.
Another day, {player}. We know your name now.
I'll tell the others you were quick. They'll want to see for themselves.

fight.hurt.text: Ngh! You'll pay for that in scales.
Lucky. You won't be lucky twice.
Is that how you crack stone? Hard and stupid?
That stung. I'll remember it. We remember everything.
You've had practice hitting small things, haven't you?
Again? Go on. There are plenty more of us.
Ow! That's going on your count.
Hit me all you like. Stone doesn't bruise.
Oof. Good arm. Pity about the rest of you.
Hah! Is that all a pick-arm's good for?
My scales! Do you know how long those take to grow?
A Warden doesn't fall to one swing, child.

fight.molt.text: Enough skin. Let's see the real me.
You've cracked the shell. Now meet what's inside.
Off it comes. All of it. Every scrap.
Molt and swarm! Molt and swarm!
Nothing left to hide. That's when we're at our worst.
Lighter now. Faster now. Worse for you.
The Mother sheds her skin each winter. Now I shed mine.
You wanted to see the silverfish? Here it is.
Out of the old skin, into the old fury.

fight.win.text: Down you go. The stone has you now.
One for our side of the count, at last.
Lie still. Now you know how it feels.
Sleep, stone-breaker. The little ones will tidy up.
Tell your bed what happened. Then stay out of our stone.
You fell like a cracked block. Very satisfying.
Next time, step around the small things.
Tell them a {rank} did this. Tell everyone.
That's one. We're a patient people. We have time for the rest.

hideout.elder.text: The coffer stays shut, {player}. You don't.
Generations of silver in that box. You thought it was unguarded?
I have slept on this hoard since before you were born. I sleep lightly.
Every scale in the coffer was shed by one of us. None of them were yours.
You've come a long way down. It's further back up.
The little ones told me you were coming. They tell me everything.
So you found the bottom of the burrow. Look around. Remember it.
Put down what you were reaching for.
Come here and meet the Silvertail.
The elder is away. I'm what's left. Unlucky you.

hideout.reseal.text: Wake me if they come back.
They'll be back. They always come back.
Not even worth a shard. Goodnight.

hideout.wake.text: Who let a stone-breaker in here?
Mm? Visitors. Nobody told me there'd be visitors.
I was having such a nice molt, too.
You walked right past the lookout. Of course you did.
Shells, everyone. Up. We have company.
You're tracking dirt on the mark.
Do you knock on every rock you find? Clearly.
Every wall in here is listening. Every wall in here is one of us.
Fresh out of the shell and already annoyed.
Shh. You'll wake the others. Too late.
You came all the way down here to die in the dark? Bold.
Up, up! Knives out, it's a guest!
Ah, a sparring partner. You'll do.
Too close to my shell. Much too close.
I just polished these scales. Let's see them fly.
A rude waking. I'll be rude back.

kin.mother.text: Kin. You've heard? Someone went down to {mother}'s hollow and killed her. Watch the stairs.
Keep your mask on tight. There's a stone-breaker about who murdered {mother}.
If you see {mother}'s killer, kin, don't be brave. Send word through the walls.
They say the one who killed {mother} walks this very road. I'm almost hoping to meet them.
Grim days, kin. {mother} in the stone, and her killer walking free.
Did you feel it when {mother} went? Like the whole hill shivered.
Keep your eyes open. {mother}'s killer won't be wearing a mask, I'd wager.
The Hollow's quiet without {mother}. I keep listening for her.

kin.whisper.text: Keep your mask on, cousin. There's a stone-breaker two hills east with a pick worn down to a nub. Warden Grisel says that one's ours.
The count's past nine thousand this season. Grisel wants every mark scratched into the wall before the thaw.
Have you heard? Someone swears they saw her. The Silver Mother, down past the old library. Nobody believes it, and nobody can stop talking about it.
Want to know how to tell a real villager from one of us? Real villagers grumble about the weather. We never do. Weather is a surface worry.
Don't eat bread where anyone can see. Real villagers drop crumbs. We don't, and the sharp ones notice.
If anyone asks, you're a fletcher from the river village. Everyone's a fletcher this month. Grisel's idea.
Steer clear of iron golems. They don't know what we are, but they know they don't like it.
That one with the shining pick, who cleared out the old fortress? Seven hundred little ones in a single night. Grisel wants that one alive. For a while.
The Shardcasters are moulting early this year. Scales everywhere. Sweep up after yourself, cousin; surface folk find them and ask questions.
Some say the Mother isn't one of us at all. Some say she's the first silverfish, grown huge and old in the deep. I say don't say either where a Warden can hear.
Five sat down in the dust. You know the story. What they don't tell the young ones is that only four stood up.
Lie down in a bed now and then, if anyone's watching. Real villagers sleep at night. The walls are for later.
Don't stand about on gravel in your disguise. It shifts under us and gives us away. Stone, cousin. Always stone.
Stone that breaks too easily gets noticed these days. Tell the young ones to stop hiding in the shallow seams.
Keep clear of cats. Every cat in every village knows exactly what we are, and not one of them will say.
Grisel's in a foul temper. Somebody slipped their mask in front of a wandering trader. The trader's llamas haven't been seen since.
There's a new name on the count. {player}. Don't look so surprised, cousin. Everybody ends up on the count.
The Mother sent word. Nobody knows how. Three words, scratched on the inside of a stone somebody split open: keep the count.
Bring the Warden silver scales, not emeralds. Emeralds are for pretending.
New, aren't you? Walk slower. Real villagers dawdle. We walk as if the ground might open, because it might.
The tally's kept in the wall behind the old spawner. Scratch your marks small. Small is how we live.
Pell swears that if you whisper the motto into a crack, the little ones whisper it back. Pell swears a great many things.
Heard about the stone-breaker who built a whole house of cobblestone? Every block of it dug out of our hills. We're still deciding how to feel.
Grisel cracked the Silvertail at a Scuttler last night for laughing during the count. Missed. Laughed too. Then went very quiet.

mother.avenge.text: This is for {mother}. All of it.
{mother} raised me from the husk. You'll answer for her.
The stone remembers {mother}. So will you, briefly.
I've waited on this road for you since {mother} fell.
{mother} is cold because of you. Let's even that.
The count has one name at the top now. Yours.
Every wall weeps for {mother}. Let's give them something to cheer.
I owe {mother} a stone-breaker. You'll do.
The others may let you walk. I'm not the others.
Mother-killer. Say it to my face, then.
Every scale I throw has {mother}'s name on it.
I knelt to {mother} for twenty winters. Kneel to me.

mother.greet.text: Funny thing. The rocks have been whispering about a traveler who went down an old stair and came back up alone.
Out here? On your own? After what you did to {mother}? Brave. Or stupid.
I know that walk. You've been somewhere deep, haven't you? Somewhere a Mother sleeps.
Everyone on this road has heard about {mother}. Everyone. Did you know that?
You've got silver dust on your boots. Old silver. I'd know it anywhere.
Strange times. They say {mother} went cold. They say someone helped her along.
Sit a while, {player}. I've been waiting to see your face since {mother} fell.
Don't mind me. I'm only a traveler. A traveler who knew {mother}.
They're singing about you in the walls, {player}. Not kindly.
You're the one, aren't you? The one who went down to {mother}.
Fine weather today. Was it fine weather when you killed {mother}?
I won't pretend I don't know you. {mother}'s killer has a certain look about them.

mother.leave.text: That's all you get. Into the dust I go.
Mind the road, {player}. Not all of us are as kind.
I'll tell them I saw you. I'll tell them you talked.
Enough talk. The walls are waiting.
Don't come looking. You won't like who you find.
Back to the stone. Remember me kindly, or don't.

mother.provoked.text: So that's how it is. Fine.
I offered you the road. You wanted the stone.
Truce over. Your choice, not mine.
You'd strike someone who let you be? {mother} was right about your kind.
I gave you mercy. You gave me a reason.

mother.reply.deny.text: I don't know what you mean.

mother.reply.proud.text: I did. And I'd do it again.
She fought well. I did better.
And you're next, if you like.

mother.reply.sorry.text: I wish it had gone another way.
I didn't know what she was.

mother.sleeper.text: It's the one who killed {mother}! Up, all of you!
{mother}'s killer, in our burrow? Shells off!
You came to do here what you did to {mother}. Not while I'm awake.
Wake up! The stone-breaker who killed {mother} is here!
I dreamt of you. You had {mother}'s dust on your hands.
Not another Mother. Not this one. Not while I breathe.
They warned us. {mother}'s killer comes down every stair.

mother.yield.text: {mother} is in the stone now. I won't follow her there today.
Anyone who can best {mother} can walk where they like. Go on.
I'm no fool, {player}. I saw what was left of the Hollow.
Keep your blade down and I'll keep mine down. Talk, if you want.
{mother} fought you and lost. I'd lose faster.
The clan's law: whoever fells a Mother walks free a season. Lucky you.
I won't fight you. I won't forgive you either.
You've nothing to fear from me today. Ask what you like.
I loved {mother}. I like breathing more.
Fine. You win. Talk to me, then, before I change my mind.
Put it away. I'm not here to die for {mother}.
The stone's quieter since {mother} went. Strange. Peaceful, almost.
Let's not. I've seen enough shells crack this season.
You killed {mother}. You can have the road. I'll keep my life.
Knives away. You've won. This time.
Keep your distance and I'll keep mine. Friendly-like.
I've buried one Mother this year. I won't bury myself as well.

reveal.first.text: We are in the stone. We were always in the stone.
Small. Grey. Everywhere. And you never once looked down.
Every stone you break, we count.
You cannot stamp out what lives inside the world.
Strike the stone, and the stone strikes back.
We were here before your pick. We will be here after.
Hidden in plain stone. Patient as the deep.

reveal.taunt.curious.text: You wanted to know about me? I was waiting for you. That's all I ever do.
Questions, questions. Here's an answer: we are in the stone.
Asking is a bad habit. Digging is a worse one. You do both.
Want to know where I'm from? Under your feet. Always under your feet.
Curious, are we? Then come and see what's under the skin.
Want to know what I do? I count stone-breakers. You're next on the tally.
Want to know who I am? Someone you've walked past a hundred times.
Ask the walls about me. They'll tell you. They're full of us.
Curious! Five miners were curious once. Look what it made of them.
Here's one for free: you were never alone out here. Not once.

reveal.taunt.polite.text: Such lovely manners. The last stone-breaker had lovely manners too.
Kind words! The little ones you crushed never got any.
Polite to my face. And to all the faces under your boots?
So courteous. I'll be courteous too. I'll make it quick. Mostly.
A gentle one! It's always the gentle ones who swing hardest at small things.
Good day to you too. It's about to get a good deal worse.
You were nice. I was nice. Only one of us was lying.
Sweet of you. Now hold still, stone-breaker.
Manners won't save you, but I do admire them. Briefly.
Thank you kindly. Now, shall we settle your count?

reveal.taunt.rude.text: Strike a stranger on the road? Now I know you're a stone-breaker.
Swing first, ask never. Just the way you dig.
That's how you greet folk? That's how you greet everything, isn't it?
You can't crack this stone with one blow. It takes a few hundred, as you well know.
Barbarian. A few kind words and I'd have let you live a little longer.
Oh, we're skipping the talk? Suits me. I hate the talking part.
Swinging at old folk on the road now? Lucky for you, I'm not old folk.
Hit first, eh? That's the stone-breaker way. Now let me show you ours.
You struck dust. Strike again; there's plenty more where that came from.

reveal.taunt.suspicious.text: Sharp eyes! Not sharp enough, but sharp.
Off, am I? Well spotted. Pity it's too late to matter.
Clever. Most never notice. Most never get the chance to.
Suspicious? Good. Fear's the only manners a stone-breaker ever learns.
You smelt the stone on me. Clever nose. Shame about the rest of you.
Right you are. I'm no villager. Well. Not only.
You saw through the stone. Now see what's under it.
Trust your gut. It's telling you to run, and for once it's right.
Caught out! Oh, I do hate that. I'll take it out on you.
You knew, and you still came close. Brave, or just slow?

reveal.taunt.timeout.text: Nothing to say? Then let me do the talking.
Silent? The stone's silent too, right before it bites.
Leaving so soon? We were only getting to know you.
Walk away from me? Nobody walks away from the stone.
Quiet one. We like quiet. Quiet is how we got this close.
Shy? Never mind. I already know all I need to about you.
No answer? Fine. I've waited in walls for years. I won't wait on you.
Turning your back on a stranger. You'll learn. Briefly.

truce.bye.text: Into the stone, then. Don't look for me.
Go well, stone-breaker. Watch the walls.
That's enough for one day. Enough for a lifetime, maybe.
I'll see you on the road. You won't see me.
Farewell, {player}. Tell nobody I was kind.
Off you go. And no more stairs, all right?

truce.clan.text: We are in the stone. That's the whole of it. Every wall, every road, every cellar you've ever slept over.
There are more of us than you'd think. Your baker. Your ferryman. That nice old shepherd. Maybe.
We count. Every silverfish you crush is a mark against your name. Some of you have very long names.
Scuttlers run the roads. Shardcasters keep the camps. The Wardens keep the young ones in line. And the Mothers keep everyone.
A Warren is a hill with a Mother under it. A den is a few of us and a fire. I like dens. Less climbing.
We sleep standing up in our old shells. It's warm, and nobody bothers you. Mostly.
The mark? A silverfish seen from above. Feelers, segments, three tails. You'll find it everywhere we've ever lived.
We were villagers once. Some of us still are, by day.
We don't hate you, stone-breaker. We just remember you. From the outside it looks the same.
Every Warren has its Mother. Every Mother has her coffer. Every coffer has the mark. That's the clan.

truce.enough.text: That's more than I've said to anyone in years. I'm done.
Enough questions. The walls are calling me home.
You've had your answers. I've had my curiosity. We're even.
No more. If the others knew I'd talked this long...

truce.greet.text: Well? You've got my attention. Use it before I think better of it.
Talking, is it? All right. I've never spoken to a Mother-killer before.
Go on, then. Ask. I might even answer.
Strange. A season ago I'd have had your throat. Now we're chatting.
Say your piece. The stone can wait a moment.
I'm listening. Keep your hands where I can see them.
Ask me anything. Except where I sleep.
Make it quick. The others won't like me talking to you.

truce.hideout.text: There's a burrow {where}, {far}. You didn't hear it from me.
Head {where}. It's {far}. You'll know the place by the smell of cold ash and old silver.
{where}, {far}, if you must know. Don't wake the little ones too rudely.
Some of my kin sleep {where}. It's {far}. Watch the lookout; it's always the friendliest face.
I can feel my kin {where}, {far}. I'd stay away, if I were you. You won't.
{where}. And if anyone asks, you found it by yourself.

truce.mother.text: {mother} was the oldest thing in that Warren. Older than the stair. She molted more times than you've had birthdays.
She raised half of us out of the husk. Fed us, named us, taught us to curl up small and listen to the rock.
{mother} never left the Hollow. Not once in thirty winters. She didn't need to. The walls brought her everything.
She could hear a pickaxe three valleys over. She'd tell us whose it was, and how many little ones it had killed.
Some say she was one of the miners who sat down in the stronghold dust. Others say she was the first silverfish's daughter. I believe both.
{mother} sang to the brood every night. You'd never know it from the Keen. It's the same voice.
Every Mother takes a new name at her last molt. {mother} was hers. I never learned the old one.
She was kind to us. Not to anyone else. But to us.
She made the coffer. Every scale in it is one of ours, shed and kept. She could tell you whose, for each one.
{mother} used to say the stone is patient, and so are we. I suppose you were more patient.

truce.nohideout.text: Nowhere near. We've moved on from these parts. Can't think why.
None close. The stone's empty round here.
Nowhere you'll find. I'm not that grateful.
Far from here. Farther than you'd want to walk.

truce.why.text: The clan has a law older than the Warrens: whoever fells a Mother walks free for a season. Not forgiven. Free.
Because you'd win. I saw what you did to {mother}. I'm not stupid enough to want that.
The others will fight you. Let them. Someone has to be left to remember her.
I'm tired. Maybe that's the truth. Shedding skins, sleeping in walls, counting the dead. I'm tired.
{mother} wouldn't want her children thrown at you one by one. She was cleverer than that.
Because you talked to me first. Nobody talks to us. They just swing.
I wanted to see what kind of person kills a Mother. You look disappointingly ordinary.
Don't mistake it for kindness. I'm letting you be. That's all.
